author: Agnete Fairwind
pages:
#First Day

At last I have found the entrance my grandfather spoke of: a crack in the cliff face hidden behind a frozen waterfall. Inside, the walls are carved with spiral patterns, and the air smells of old dust and older stone. I have supplies for five days. More than enough.

#Second Day

The passages go deeper than I thought. I found a hall of stone coffins, all empty, which I did not like. I found a lever, which I did not pull. I am proud of that. Grandfather always said to never pull the lever.

I have marked my path with chalk on the walls.

#Third Day

My chalk marks are gone. Or rather, they are there, but they are pointing the wrong way. Someone, or something, has redrawn them.

I am trying not to panic. I have food and water and a good lantern. I will simply be careful.

#Fourth Day

I pulled the lever.

I do not want to talk about it.

#Fifth Day

I can see daylight. A shaft in the ceiling of a great round chamber, too high to climb. Beside me is a chest that I have not dared to open. On the wall are carvings of a dragon, and beneath the dragon, a word I almost understand.

If I do not come back, whoever reads this: the treasure is real. So is everything else.
